title: How to make your haircut last longer between barber visits
description: Practical tips from 3D Cutz in Norwich to keep your cut looking sharp longer — washing, styling and small maintenance between visits.

content.heading: Start with the right cut and clear instructions
paragraphs: A haircut that suits your daily routine will naturally last longer. Be honest with your barber about how often you want to maintain the style, how much time you spend styling each morning, and whether you exercise or wear hats regularly.

Ask your barber at 3D Cutz (19 Prince of Wales Road, Norwich NR1 1BD) for small tweaks that improve longevity — slightly more length on top, a softer graduation, or a neatened neckline can reduce how quickly a cut looks untidy.

content.heading: Wash and dry with care
paragraphs: Over-washing strips natural oils and can make hair look limp; most people benefit from washing every other day or using a gentle shampoo only a few times a week. Use a conditioner to keep hair manageable and reduce frizz, especially if you have thicker or drier hair.

When drying, pat rather than rub with a towel and use a brush or comb to shape the hair while it’s damp. If you blow-dry, use a medium heat and a brush to set the direction — that helps styles hold and means less reshaping later.

content.heading: Choose products and tools that suit your style
paragraphs: Lightweight creams, styling lotions or a small amount of matte paste often give hold without weighing hair down. Apply products to damp hair for even distribution and finish by directing the hair with a comb or fingers to maintain the intended shape.
Avoid heavy waxes or greasy pomades if you want a natural look that lasts; salt sprays can add texture and grip for styles that need to sit well between visits.

content.heading: Simple upkeep between visits
paragraphs: Refresh your cut daily by dampening and combing or using a styling product to tame stray hairs. For necklines and tiny stray hairs, a quick tidy with a personal trimmer helps, but take care — small mistakes are easy and quick for your barber to fix but hard to correct at home.

If you need a quick tidy-up, pop into 3D Cutz at 19 Prince of Wales Road for a touch-up rather than trying a major home haircut. Regular short visits or a slightly longer interval with a slightly longer style are both fine strategies to keep your look sharp.
